text:
Growing in densities, in such a way

that in a nearby century you will be solid.

Giant blue plinth with soft rose

wetting your skin in twilight.


All your malleable softness,

that now supports our bodies,

will set among its fragrant salts

and you will be whole, a polished track.


Who will go over your ground, then so tight

as now it is of oily liquid?

What creatures will you hear sliding,

drunk with you, through your infinity?


I sense you in the stone of yourself,

mineral your presence, which slowly,

fugitive, evaporates gently

its bodily thickness of seaweed and iodine.




The Poems of Mar Menor, 1959

translation.title: Growing in Densities, in Such a Way...
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the Mar Menor imagined becoming mineral, solid, and still fragrant with salt.
